# Three Consecutive Odds.

@example 15, 3 and 21 are odd and stand side by side.
[8,15,3,21,4]
=> true

@example Five of the numbers are odd, but an even number cuts every run of odd ones after at most two.
[5,9,2,7,11,6,13]
=> false

@example Two elements are too few for a window of three.
[3,3]
=> false

# One element, and two odd elements.
[1]
=> false

[999,1]
=> false

# The shortest array that qualifies.
[1,1,1]
=> true

# No odd number at all.
[2,4,6]
=> false

[1000,1000,1000,1000]
=> false

# The window at the very start, and at the very end.
[7,1,3,2,4,6]
=> true

[2,4,6,8,999,1,5]
=> true

# Runs of two odd numbers, again and again: a count that isn't reset at an
# even number goes wrong.
[1,3,2,5,7,2,9,11,2,13,15]
=> false

# Odd and even alternate: many odd numbers, never three in a row.
[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]
=> false

# A run longer than three.
[2,1,1,1,1,1,2]
=> true

# The values themselves don't have to follow one another.
[999,1,501]
=> true

# The bounds: 1000 is even, 999 and 1 are odd.
[1000,999,1,1000]
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[12,5,4,4,3,5,1]
=> true

@gen 2 small
[5,2,1,12,8]
=> false

@gen 3 small
[5,4,8,2,10,4,8,2]
=> false

@gen 4 small
[9,7,1,12]
=> true

@gen 5 small
[9,7,8,9,5,11]
=> true

@gen 6 small
[3,11]
=> false

@gen 7 small
[3,9,9,11,5,5]
=> true
